## Verdicts

Spec/integration: **CHANGES REQUIRED**. Quality: **CHANGES REQUIRED**.

Actionable findings: **1 P1**. No P0, P2, or P3 findings.

## [P1] Align the workflow restore verifier with the extended selection-scoped ceiling

Location: `.github/workflows/boat-blob-e2e.yml:338`.

The workflow now supplies 480 seconds for `all-upcoming`, and the worker correctly writes that configured value into `manifest['max_seconds']`. The downstream restored-manifest budget guard still requires `0 < manifest['max_seconds'] <= 240`. Consequently every new extended-budget run with a manifest reaches `COHORT_MANIFEST_BUDGET_CONFLICT`, including valid completed/bounded runs after receipts have already been published. The new production path cannot complete its required restore verification.

Apply the same selection-dependent ceiling in this verifier: 480 only for `all-upcoming`, 240 otherwise, while retaining all write/read/file/identity checks. Add a focused no-network regression for the verifier boundary: valid all-upcoming/480 accepted, next-per-venue/480 rejected, 481 rejected, and existing 240 cases accepted. This should exercise the workflow verification predicate, since the current new tests cover the worker only.

## Other assessed behavior and test meaning

- `scripts/publish_research_cohort.py:124,133–136` keeps the default 240 seconds and permits an explicit finite numeric value up to 480 only after validating `selection='all-upcoming'`. Default/next-per-venue still rejects 241, booleans remain invalid, and all-upcoming rejects 481. No other worker execution behavior was changed in the diff.
- The workflow environment expression selects 480 only for exact `all-upcoming`, otherwise 240, and the CLI argument consumes that value. Existing application/publisher pins remain 325 in this prepared code; root explicitly defers their successor integration to the later CI/Preview/pinned-workflow review, so this known pending gate is not counted as a separate finding or treated as ready for dispatch.
- The new 132-preserved-race synthetic test addresses the actual failure mechanism. With the same two-second-per-transport fixture and immutable prior receipt map, 240 seconds saves no new tail receipts, while 480 seconds preserves all 132 and completes the remaining 24. It asserts 181 GET reads, 24 POSTs, 410 simulated seconds, exactly 49 JSON files, no pending tail, and unchanged old receipts. These are meaningful externally visible coverage/budget/preservation checks rather than only testing the changed ceiling expression.
- The second new test proves that accepting 480 does not disable the monotonic stop: once elapsed reaches 480 after a preserved lookup, the worker stops with two reads, no POSTs, one preserved receipt, and the honest two-race pending tail. The invalid-options test preserves next-per-venue's 240 ceiling and adds the all-upcoming 481 rejection.
- Inspection of the named existing budget helper confirms unchanged monotonic/read caps and HTTP reserve checks. No source acquisition, write-slot/read/file expansion, receipt replacement, cutoff/JST weakening, OIDC/trust/permissions change, concurrency change, or job-timeout change appears in this diff. The sole detected integration mismatch is the restored-manifest 240 cap above.

## Scope and evidence limits

Read `artifacts/local/cohort480-review.diff` once, then inspected only the named worker selection/time-budget and workflow restore-budget integration boundaries. Root reports two RED `COHORT_TIME_LIMIT_INVALID` regressions followed by 32 passing caller tests; those results were not independently rerun. The synthetic 410-second figure is simulated transport time, not a wall-clock production-duration claim.

# Independent review: extended-run scoped OIDC renewal

## Verdicts

Spec/auth-failure boundary: **CHANGES REQUIRED**. Quality: **CHANGES REQUIRED**.

Actionable findings: **1 P1**. No P0, P2, or P3 findings.

## [P1] Keep issuer HTTP404 failures out of prediction-absence classification

Location: `scripts/publish_research_cohort.py:197` and `:225–231` (renewal implementation at `:181–192`).

`read()` now calls `authorized()`, which may call `workflow_session(commit)`. Existing prediction lookup wraps the entire `read()` call and classifies any `RuntimeError('DAY_PUBLISH_HTTP_404')` as a missing forecast. The same `workflow_session` obtains its issuer token through `get_json`; an issuer HTTP404 is also normalized to precisely that error (`scripts/publish_race_updates.py:117–118`, `scripts/publish_day_feed.py:53–55`).

Consequently an OIDC renewal HTTP404 can become `missing=True` without a business prediction lookup. The worker can allocate a new publication request slot and attempt renewal again for POST, rather than stopping on the authentication failure. If that later renewal succeeds, it can send a publication despite never establishing missingness for that candidate. This violates the intended renewal-failure stop/absence boundary.

Scope the missing-forecast catch to the business prediction transport only, or normalize renewal failures to a distinct fixed/redacted auth error before they can reach that catch. Add a no-network regression where the second `workflow_session` raises `RuntimeError('DAY_PUBLISH_HTTP_404')`; require STOPPED, no next business lookup/POST/request slot, and attempts2/ready1. Preserve genuine business-prediction 404 handling.

## Other assessed behavior

- Renewal is confined to explicit extended budgets (`max_seconds > 240`), which the reviewed selection guard permits only for all-upcoming. Default and 240-second runs do not gain periodic renewal. The same configured application commit is passed into the existing session helper, preserving issuer validation, audience, commit header, both authorization headers, and existing server-side expiry/trust checks.
- The 180-second monotonic threshold leaves room within the supplied five-minute token lifetime for bounded issuer/business calls. Before renewal, the worker reserves the issuer's 30 seconds plus the required business reserve. It rechecks time before business I/O. The business-read cap is checked before authorization and is unaffected by issuer calls, which are separately counted.
- Reconstructed requests retain URL, bytes, and method while applying the newly returned session headers/opener. POST renewal occurs after request backup and before the unchanged 60-second reserve and fresh actual JST/cutoff check; a renewal that crosses cutoff retains the backed-up request without sending a POST. Existing write-slot/pending accounting remains honest.
- Initial and renewal attempts/readiness are distinct manifest counters, with failed attempts not counted ready. No token, issuer URL, token claims, or credential values are recorded. Existing failure redaction remains in place, subject to the issuer404 classification finding above.
- The new successful-renewal test models a five-minute token lifetime over the real slow preserved-prefix fixture, checks the same commit, and rejects expired authorization headers. It expects three sessions and unchanged 181 business reads/24 POSTs. Failure and renewal-crosses-cutoff tests cover stopping/redaction and no-post behavior, but the failure test uses a generic RuntimeError and misses the issuer404/business404 collision identified here.
- The prior selection-scoped workflow restore fix remains present. No OIDC subject/audience/environment/permissions, server expiry validation, 24-write/313-read/49-file bounds, per-call timeout, job timeout, or serial/concurrency change appears in this diff.

## Scope and execution limits

Read `artifacts/local/cohort480-auth-review.diff` once. Inspected only the named worker authorization/read/POST/error integration and the existing `workflow_session`/`get_json` definitions needed to trace issuer errors. The maintainer lifetime reference supplied by root was not fetched because this review explicitly prohibits network access.

Root reports three RED failures followed by 37 focused caller/workflow tests passing. The 957-test full-suite PASS preceded this auth addition and is not final-auth-head verification; the new 960-test suite was pending at the supplied boundary. No results were independently rerun here.

No tests, compilation, helper import/execution, credentials, network/browser/source requests, dispatch, storage writes, Git mutation, subagents, repository/root-doc edits, workflow/trust changes, or operational evidence changes were performed. Only this independent review report was written. Exact final CI/READY, the later second-checkout-only workflow pin review, and fresh operational execution/reconciliation gates remain root-owned; this review grants no extended dispatch authority.
